_about: Analyst research snapshot. Each entry was found with a live web search on 2026-10-04 and the source pages are linked. Notes are short paraphrases written by the analyst, not copied text. Open the URLs to verify. Re-run live search in the app to refresh.
method: Analyst web research session (search engine), sources opened and summarised

sources.title: 1200 V Bare Die Silicon Carbide MOSFETs – Gen 4
sources.note: Sells industrial-qualified 1200 V silicon carbide MOSFETs as bare die; site lists industrial motor drives, EV powertrain and charging as target applications.

sources.title: 650 V Bare Die SiC MOSFETs – Gen 3
sources.note: 650 V SiC bare die positioned for industrial power supplies, EV charging systems and energy storage.

sources.title: Wolfspeed completes financial restructuring (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1)
sources.note: Emerged from Chapter 11 on 29 Sep 2025; total debt cut by roughly 70% and maturities pushed to 2030; describes a vertically integrated 200 mm US manufacturing footprint.

sources.title: Wolfspeed cuts quarterly loss after CapEx slashed during restructuring
sources.note: Filed for Chapter 11 on 30 Jun 2025 and exited 29 Sep 2025; reported negative non-GAAP gross margin for the quarter; says it kept supplying customers during the process.

sources.title: BT1M120 Bare Die — 1,200 V SiC bare die MOSFETs for inverter modules
sources.note: 1200 V silicon carbide trench MOSFETs supplied as bare die for inverter modules around 800 V; qualification based on AEC-Q101 plus SiC-specific validation; front-side metallisation for sintering.

sources.title: SiC bare die portfolio 750 V (BT2M075)
sources.note: Also offers 750 V SiC bare die for ~400 V inverter modules, chargers and DC/DC converters; portfolio spans bare die, discretes and power modules.

sources.title: Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFETs Bare Die
sources.note: EliteSiC MOSFET bare die (1200 V M3e listed) optimised for traction inverters, DC-DC converters and off-board chargers.

sources.title: Silicon Carbide technology — EliteSiC
sources.note: Claims end-to-end SiC manufacturing and offers SiC power modules for energy storage and industrial drives as well as industrial power supplies.

sources.title: onsemi EliteSiC (distributor product highlight)
sources.note: Distributor page notes 100% avalanche testing of dies, automotive-grade qualification and fully integrated manufacturing from powder to product.

sources.title: AT&S Worldwide
sources.note: High-end PCB maker serving industrial and automotive; its Austrian and Indian plants focus on small/medium series for those sectors; portfolio includes insulated metallic substrate boards for heat management.

sources.title: AT&S – First choice for advanced solutions (careers)
sources.note: Production sites in Austria, India, China and Korea plus a new site in Malaysia; roughly 14,000 employees.

sources.title: Premium Heavy Copper PCB Manufacturer
sources.note: Heavy-copper PCBs for power electronics; states IPC-A-610 workmanship and cites a 50 kW solar inverter board case. Plant footprint and production scale are not stated on the page.

sources.title: Thick Copper PCB Board Prototype & Manufacturer
sources.note: 4–20 oz copper boards for high-current inverters, DC-DC converters and industrial power supplies; marketing blog rather than a capability statement.

sources.title: Toray commercializes advanced grade of Torayfan capacitor film
sources.note: Began mass production of a biaxially oriented polypropylene capacitor film with higher thermal and voltage resistance for electrified-vehicle capacitors; says polypropylene film capacitors are core parts of inverter circuits.

sources.title: Toray to boost Torayfan polypropylene film capacity at Tsuchiura
sources.note: Further capacity increase for automotive capacitor film at its Tsuchiura plant (Japan), after a 2022 expansion; film capacitors serve inverter circuits.

sources.title: Polypropylene BOPP film for capacitor
sources.note: Claims to be an early maker of polypropylene film for power capacitors with 30+ years in production; metallised film offered for power electronics and EV battery/motor management. The site also markets packaging films, so the capability claim needs confirmation.
